newsitem.title: USA: Panasonic signs DVCPRO contract with NBC.
newsitem.headline: Panasonic signs DVCPRO contract with NBC.

text.p: Panasonic Broadcast & Digital Systems Co said Thursday that NBC has signed a multi-year, multi-million dollar pact to convert its 11 owned and operated television stations to Panasonic DVCPRO digital component recording equipment.
The DVCPRO is a quarter-inch video tape format that allows for smaller, lighter equipment.
A Panasonic spokesman declined to reveal the dollar amount of the deal.
Panasonic, a division of Matsushita Electric Industrial Co's North American subsidiary, had signed a pact in April valued at $24 million to convert 13 CBS-owned stations.
Panasonic said in a statement that more than 17,000 DVCPRO units have been delivered worldwide and that it expects to make deliveries of 10,000 units in the United States in 1997.
NBC is owned by General Electric Co. CBS is owned by Westinghouse Electric Corp.
